chunks: I asked Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him)
about the Sanctuary and its boundary markers — how some came to be closer than others and some farther apart

He said: When God, Mighty and Majestic, caused Adam to descend from Paradise, he descended upon Mount Abu Qubays. He complained to his Lord of loneliness and that he could no longer hear what he used to hear in Paradise.

So God, Mighty and Majestic, sent down upon him a red ruby, and he placed it at the site of the House (Kaaba). Adam used to circumambulate it, and its light reached the locations of the boundary markers — thus the boundary markers were set according to its light, and God made it a Sanctuary.
A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abu Hammam Ismail ibn Hammam al-Kindi, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him): similar to this.

key_terms.أَبُو قُبَيْس: Mount Abu Qubays — a mountain near Mecca where Adam is said to have first descended after his expulsion from Paradise
key_terms.أَعْلَام: boundary markers/signs — the physical pillars that demarcate the limits of the Haram
key_terms.الْحَرَم: the Sanctuary — the sacred inviolable zone surrounding Mecca whose boundaries define where certain hajj and umra rituals are binding
key_terms.الْوَحْشَة: loneliness/desolation — the spiritual isolation Adam felt after being separated from the sounds and presence of Paradise
key_terms.يَاقُوتَة حَمْرَاء: red ruby — a luminous gem sent by God that served as the origin of the Kaaba's physical foundation and demarcated the Haram by its radiance

ai.seo_question: Why are the boundaries of the Meccan Haram (sanctuary) at unequal distances from the Kaaba?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (AS) provides the cosmic origin of the Meccan Sanctuary (Haram) and explains why its boundaries are irregular — varying distances from the Kaaba. Adam, upon descending from Paradise to Mount Abu Qubays near Mecca, complained to God of isolation and the loss of the celestial sounds he heard in Paradise. God sent down a radiant red ruby which Adam placed at the site of the future Kaaba; the light of the ruby defined the sacred boundaries that persist to this day. This narrative situates the Haram's sanctity at the very dawn of human history, linking Adam's fall, the first act of tawaf, and divine luminescence to the physical boundaries Muslims observe during hajj.
